Subject: Procurement: SLO measurement questionnaire

Marissa —

Thanks for taking our procurement questionnaire. A few follow-ups from our side so we can finalize the uptime/latency section for legal and SRE review. Could you confirm the details below? We put the items we care most about first.

1) Uptime definition: is downtime calculated at region-level or global? How do you handle partial-region degradations?
2) Measurement window & sampling: what is the rolling window (30d/90d) used for availability calculation and what sampling cadence do you use for synthetic checks vs production request sampling?
3) Latency targets: where do p50/p95/p99 measurements come from (edge vs origin), and how do you treat spike-outs (single-request anomalies)?
4) Alerting & escalation: what thresholds will trigger a P1 and what is the on-call paging policy? Will we get immediate paging and a public incident page?
5) Customer access: can we get a read-only Grafana link with raw timeseries for availability and percentiles? What retention do you provide for metrics and request logs?
6) Maintenance & exceptions: do scheduled maintenance windows count against SLO? If we request a temporary SLA exception (e.g., heavy migration), what is the approval path and how is availability recalculated?

I've attached our internal questionnaire (TW_procurement_slo_questions.xlsx) with the fields we need filled. Could you return answers and any supporting artifacts (dashboards, sample monthly report) by EOD Thursday PST?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call if you prefer to walk through.

—Anna

Head of Procurement, TicketWave

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Anna — thanks for the clear list. Answers below at a high level; we've attached a one-page summary and a sample monthly uptime report. If that looks good we can fill the spreadsheet itself.

1) Uptime definition: availability is calculated at the regional level (region = cloud availability zone group). We report both regional and global availability; contractual measurement is region-scoped by default. Partial-region degradations are evaluated by the percentage of traffic impacted — if >5% of your routed requests are affected we count it as a regional degradation for SLA purposes.

2) Measurement window & sampling: our standard contractual window is 30-day rolling availability for monthly SLAs; enterprise customers can elect a 90-day smoothing window. For measurement we use two sources: continuous production telemetry (sampled at 1:1 on success/error counters for 99% of traffic) plus synthetic health probes every 30s per-region. Synthetic probe failures are tagged and reconciled against production traces during incident reviews.

3) Latency targets: percentile numbers are computed at the edge (post-ingress, pre-tokenization) to reflect end-to-end customer latency. We compute p50/p95/p99 across the production request stream and drop single-request outliers beyond 6σ for percentile stability (we keep a separate raw series for audit).

4) Alerting & escalation: default P1 triggers are region availability <99.5% over a 5m window, or sustained p99 latency above your agreed threshold for 10m. We page SRE on-call, open an incident in our status system and we provide an incident bridge with you when severity is P1. We also publish a public incident page and post-mortem for Sev2/Sev1 incidents.

5) Customer access: we can provide read-only Grafana links scoped to your account with 90d retained metrics by default, longer on request. Request logs (non-PII aggregated) are kept 30d; full trace/event export is available under a contract addendum. We'll add you to a shared dashboard and give an export-friendly monthly CSV on request.

6) Maintenance & exceptions: scheduled maintenance windows will not count against SLO if agreed 72h in advance and announced with a maintenance ticket. For ad-hoc temporary exceptions (e.g., high-throughput migration) we support time-bounded exceptions: outline the impact window, mitigation steps, and desired exclusion period and we will respond within 24 business hours with approval or a counter-proposal. Exceptions are documented and applied to the rolling window calculation as an excluded period.

Next steps: I'll fill the spreadsheet this afternoon and share the summary PDF. I'd also propose a short call tomorrow 9am PST to walk through the migration exception process — can you confirm?

Best,
Marissa

Marissa — thanks, that level of detail helps. Two quick follow-ups before the call:

- We have a planned database migration next month that will route temporary burst traffic through a new ingestion pipeline for ~48 hours. We'd like a temporary SLA exception window so that any availability drop during that migration does not count against the rolling 30-day SLO. Is a 48-hour exclusion feasible and what information do you need to approve?
- For the shared Grafana access: can we create two roles (Team ReadOnly + Oncall ReadWrite) so our SREs can set local alerts without getting account-wide write access?

I've attached a short migration plan that includes expected traffic curves. If possible we'd like the exclusion to start at 2027-10-12 00:00 UTC and end 2027-10-14 00:00 UTC.

—Anna
Attachment: migration-plan.docx (docx, 24KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Anna Reynolds <anna@ticketwave.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement: SLO measurement questionnaire & exception request

Anna — all good. We can approve a 48-hour exclusion under the following conditions:

- Exclusion window must be submitted in writing (you already did, good) and confirmed 72h before start.
- Redwood will require a conservative canary: start with 2h low-percentage traffic ramp, then 8h intermediate, then full traffic. Provide your ramp schedule and rollback criteria.
- During the window we will keep synthetic probing frequency at 30s and will not apply the exclusion to any region where production errors exceed 15% sustained for 15m — that will be treated as a Sev2 incident and not covered by the exception.
- We will log the exclusion as an audit entry and exclude the two-day window from the rolling SLA calculation. Credits (if any) will be calculated on the post-exclusion adjusted window per contract.

About Grafana roles: yes, we support per-user role mappings. We'll provision Team ReadOnly and Oncall ReadWrite scoped to the TicketWave account; Oncall write access is limited to alert definitions only (no dashboard-level editing). Aditya — can you create the dashboard invite and a read-only report template and share before Thursday?

If that sounds OK I'll have legal add the exclusion language to the quote addendum and we'll lock the timeline. Happy to join the call at 9am PST tomorrow.

—Marissa
